In Irish mythology , Fiacha ( [ ˈfʲiːəxə ] , sometimes Fiachu , Fiachra or Fiachna ) , son of Delbáeth , of the Tuatha Dé Danann , was a legendary High King of Ireland . According to the Lebor Gabála Érenn , he took the throne after his father was overthrown by Caicher son of Nama , brother of Nechtan . The Annals of the Four Masters and Geoffrey Keating say he overthrew his father himself . His mother was Ernmas . He had three daughters , Banba , Fódla , and Ériu , by his own mother . He reigned for ten years , before he and his nephew Aoi Mac Ollamain were killed in battle against Éogan of Imber .
